name: level-editor
description: In-game level editor: an Edit run mode over the real pipeline — scene round-trip, selection, bounded undo/redo (gizmo + toolbar land in Wave 4b)
postInstallNotes:
## level-editor module installed

The in-game editor stands on the run-state model in `foundation` (`GameState.RunMode` Play/Edit + `EditTimeBehavior` + the `GatedSystem` decorator) and the docs codifying "the editor is part of the game" (`docs/CORE_TENETS.md` tenet + a `foundation` run-state premise).

Live today: the scene round-trip (`SceneObjectComponent`, `Serialization/` registry + `SceneWriter`, `LoadSceneRequest` + `SceneReaderSystem`), selection (`SelectedComponent` + `SelectionSystem`, picking the frontmost sprite), and bounded undo/redo with drag-coalescing (`Undo/` — `EditorHistory`, `IEditorCommand`, create/delete/transform commands). The transform gizmo + the engine-native toolbar are Wave 4b; the headless editor-op channel is Wave 5. See `docs/level-editor/roadmap.md` for the wave map and plug-in points.

To opt a screen into editing: wrap the game-logic / physics / camera-follow systems in `GatedSystem(child, EditTimeBehavior.Freeze)`, keep render / input / cursor / `HierarchySystem` ungated (or `RunNormally`), register the editor systems (`SelectionSystem`, `EditorModeToggleSystem`, `EditorCommandSystem`, `SceneReaderSystem`) RunNormally + Edit-guarded, and flip `gameState.RunMode` to enter/exit Edit with no screen swap. The reference assembly is `MonoDreams.Examples.Core/Screens/LevelEditorScreen.cs`; the full system-by-mode policy is the interaction matrix in `docs/CORE_TENETS.md`.
